what_it_does: Modern processors have specialized 8-bit integer (INT8) hardware engines that multiply matrices very fast, but many scientific and machine learning workloads require higher precision than 8 bits to maintain numerical accuracy. This paper shows how to compute higher-precision matrix multiplications by decomposing them into multiple 8-bit operations and combining the results, allowing engineers to reuse fast hardware designed for lower precision.
method_in_detail: The work uses emulation techniques to map high-precision matrix operations onto INT8 matrix engines, exploiting the hardware's speed while maintaining the accuracy needed for the application.
